messages.author: f50fa26a0f71df3e
messages.subject: digit.curves function
parts:
Hello geomorph team,

I am using the digit.curves function to evenly space out my semi-landmarks along my curve. My curve has 21 semi-landmarks, so I set nPoints = 19 to exclude the starting/ending points. 

However, when I ran it, I get this warning: because the number of desired points exceeds the number of curve points, the number of points will be truncated to 19  

As a result, the number of semi-landmarks was automatically reduced from 21 to 19. Is there way to prevent this from happening, as I would like to maintain the same number of semilandmarks? This warning did not happen before (albeit, it was more than a year ago) when I ran the same set of scripts. 

I greatly appreciate your help!


Chris Law

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] digit.curves function
parts:
Chris,

 

I do not understand your question. You state that you have 21 total points, the first and last of which are treated as fixed. Thus, you do have 19 semilandmark points, which is what the function is trying to do.

 

Dean

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] digit.curves function
parts:
Hi Dean and Mike,

The problem is that after running digit.curves with nPoints =19, it reduces the total of points from 21 to 19. So the new curve only has 19 points (17 spaced semilandmarks and 2 fixed points). The original curve had 21 points (19 unevenly spaced semilandmarks and 2 fixed points). I want to evenly space my 21 points but the function automatically removes 2 semilandmarks for some reason. 

Hope that clarifies my question. Thanks!
